Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
213 AM PST Sat Nov 28 2026

.SYNOPSIS...28/212 AM.

A cooling trend will kick off today as the offshore flow subsides
and turns onshore. Sunday, the first in a series of storms will move
through the region. The first chance for rain will be Sunday 
afternoon through Monday. A much stronger system with heavy rain
will move through the area early Tuesday morning through at least
Wednesday morning.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-MON)...28/212 AM.

A broad shield of high clouds moving ahead of a strong storm will
bring an end to the sunny skies today. These clouds and a switch 
to onshore flow in the afternoon will bring 3 to 6 degrees of 
cooling to most areas. Despite this cooling max temps will end up 
4 to 8 degrees above normal.

On Sunday the ridge will be pushed to the east by a weak trof. It
will bring a 20-30 percent chc of light rain to the Central Coast
in the afternoon, but for the most part it will just be a cloudy
day as a grip of mid and high level clouds embedded in the
westerly flow stream overhead. There will also be weak onshore
flow which when combined with lower hgts and the cloud cover will
bring an additional 3 to 6 degrees of cooling.

Light rain will likely develop across the Central Coast Sunday
evening and then work its way to LA county by dawn. Overnight
rainfall will be less than a tenth xcp north of Morro Bay where up
a to quarter inch could fall.

Moist slightly difluent WSW flow will cover the area on Monday. It
will be a cloudy day with on again off again showers esp across
the coastal slopes and foothills. Rainfall total should not
exceed a quarter in and more than likely will be less than a 
tenth. Further cooling will bring max temps down to the mid 60s to
lower 70s.

.LONG TERM (TUE-FRI)...28/212 AM.

All eyes on the large storm that will affect the area early
Tuesday through early Wednesday. A potent 550 dam upper low will
move in from the west and then pivot to the NE into San Diego
county. This is a more unusual system and is not the more typical
cold frontal passage system with the parent low well to the north.
This track of the upper low near to or over the area will favor
convection and will produce a greater than normal threat of severe
weather. It will affect VTA and esp LA counties much more than SLO
and SBA counties. The mdls have been very consistent with this 
storms fcst (perhaps there is a slight southward trend) so 
confidence is quite high with this system.

This system carries PWATs in the 90+ percential and is traveling
across ocean waters that are 5-10 degrees warmer than normal which
will add extra low level water vapor into the storm. Rainfall
totals with this system will likely fall into the 1-3 inch for
csts/vlys and 3 to 5 inches for the coastal slopes and foothills
with the highest amounts over LA county. There is 20 percent chc 
that these numbers are an inch or two too low as much depends on
the speed and exact track of the low. Non convective rain rates 
of an inch per hour are possible with this system especially in 
the foothills and coastal slopes. Rain rates under any convective 
cell could be near 1.5 in/hr.

Residents, especially in areas that are compromised by fires in 
the last year or two should pay close attention to the forecasts 
and begin preparations to protect your property. Also, make plans 
now for possible evacuations.

The rain will taper off overnight Tuesday into early Wednesday.
Aside from a few lingering showers the day will be dry with
clearing skies and max temps in the mid 60s to lower 70s.

Thursday will feature a fast moving ridge and weak offshore flow.
Look for sunny skies and near normal temperatures.

Another low is slated to arrive Friday. Most solutions favor
totals around a quarter inch. One thing, however, ydy's solutions
had no heavier projections and now there are a few with heavier
rainfall projected. This trend will need watching.

&&

.AVIATION...28/1012Z.

At 0822Z at KLAX, There was no marine layer. There was a surface-
based inversion. The top of the inversion was at 1300 feet with a
temp of 24 deg C.

High confidence in VFR TAFs.

KLAX...High confidence in TAF. Good confidence that any east wind
component remains below 7 kts.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...28/142 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Conds will be largely below SCA levels today through 
Monday before winds and seas increase Monday night to SCA levels 
ahead of an approaching strong storm system. Winds are expected to
increase to SCA to Gale Force Tuesday and continue through 
Wednesday, along with large and increasingly hazardous seas as the
storm impacts the area. SCA winds and seas will continue 
Wednesday night, with a 50% chance of Gale Force winds.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high 
confidence in current forecast. Conds will be below SCA levels 
today through Monday evening before winds increase late Monday 
night to SCA levels ahead of an approaching strong storm system. 
Winds are expected to increase further to Gale Force Tuesday as 
the storm impacts the area. Winds and seas to SCA levels can be 
expected Tuesday night, with seas to SCA levels persisting 
Wednesday and Wednesday night.

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate 
confidence in current forecast. Through Monday evening, winds and 
seas are expected to remain below SCA levels. Winds are expected 
to increase to SCA levels Monday night ahead of an approaching 
strong storm system. Gale Force winds are expected Tuesday and 
Tuesday night as the storm impacts the region. Winds to SCA levels
are expected for the southern waters Wednesday, otherwise conds 
should be below SCA levels Wednesday and Wednesday night.

It looks very likely that there will be significant impacts over 
the coastal waters from the Pacific storm system forecast mainly 
from Monday night into Wednesday. Gale Force winds and hazardous 
seas will spread to all the coastal waters with this system, along
with the potential for squalls with thunderstorms and waterspouts.
Poor visibility in heavy rain is also expected. Mariners are 
encouraged to pay close attention to the latest forecasts and any 
future statements regarding this storm system.

&&

.BEACHES...28/142 AM.

A large, long period, west swell will continue to slowly subside
across the waters. High surf will continue through this afternoon
along the Central Coast, as well as the Ventura and Los Angeles 
County coasts. There will be many, strong rip nearly everywhere, 
strong long shore currents, some risk of sneaker waves, large 
shore pound, and coastal erosion. These conditions will lead to an
increased risk of drowning and make swimming dangerous.

In addition, an exceptionally high tide of up to 7.2 feet is 
predicted for this morning, and this will continue the threat of 
minor to moderate coastal flooding over low-lying coastal areas. A
Coastal Flood Advisory continues until 4 PM today for the Ventura
County beaches. Elsewhere, low-lying coastal areas with no 
protection from the ocean will still be vulnerable to sea water 
intrusion during the Saturday morning high tide.

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories in effect.
